findings.issue: The generic /edge/ regex also matches the word knowledge. As a result, knowledge-assistants detail renders an edge-compute laboratory visual, and multiple knowledge catalog items are incorrectly assigned edge imagery.
findings.recommendation: Replace substring heuristics with explicit content/slug image identity mappings. Validate semantic relevance in addition to distinct file counts.

findings.issue: Six distinct blog articles resolve to four visual identities. prototype aliases edge; rfq aliases knowledge.
findings.recommendation: Give each article a distinct intentional cover, shared only by that article thumbnail/detail/social preview. Do not solve by merely hue-shifting or cropping the same original.

findings.issue: Blog index hero repeats knowledge cover also assigned to two different articles.
findings.recommendation: Use a dedicated editorial masthead visual or typographic/art direction composition with clear browse controls; retain rich unique covers in the article grid.

findings.issue: Generic slug classifier collapses solution, reference-case and resource cards into knowledge, meeting or edge; same image can appear many times on a single page.
findings.recommendation: Map distinct content to meaningful visual subjects, use compact reference typography or topic diagrams where genuine photos are unavailable; preserve concept-versus-verified-evidence labeling.

findings.issue: Homepage repeats product lead photos in hero and catalog and repeats knowledge/meeting/edge between workflow explorer and journal teaser.
findings.recommendation: Keep real product imagery as evidence while use different verified product views across adjacent sections and reserve original workflow scenes for explorer; article teaser receives unique article artwork.

findings.issue: Detailed article reuse can recur in related-card area because different posts share artwork; cover SEO assignment is separate logic.
findings.recommendation: Update rendered cover, alt descriptions, OpenGraph and Twitter image mappings together; verify no own-cover duplicate among related cards.
